roster.relevance_reason: Discusses Engram-style or parametric memory mechanisms for language models.
roster.publication_status_evidence: arXiv manuscript identifier; no external publication established by the available metadata.

sort_key: causal path alignment: anchoring the optimization trajectory for controllable in-parameter knowledge editing

primary_final_assessment.claim_evidence_alignment: The manuscript's claims are well supported by the presented evidence. The diagnosis of Subject-Dominant Shortcut is backed by gradient saliency maps and causal tracing (RIE) across GPT2-XL, GPT-J, and Qwen2.5. The proposed CPA method is evaluated on COUNTERFACT RS and EVOKE across four model backbones, with ablations, mechanistic validation, and plug-and-play generalization to MEMIT and AlphaEdit. Limitations, including weaker zsRE performance and increased latency, are explicitly acknowledged.
primary_final_assessment.evaluation_assessment: The paper makes a substantive, scoped contribution: it identifies a shortcut-learning pathology in locate-then-edit knowledge editing and proposes a two-phase optimization framework (CPA) to anchor updates to relational causal paths. The method is clearly described with formal objectives and implementation details. Evaluation is meaningful and appropriate for the contribution type, including multiple model families, two benchmarks, ablations, mechanistic validation, and generalization to other editors. Claims are justified by the reported results, and limitations are candidly discussed.
primary_final_assessment.limitations: The method shows weaker efficacy and generalization on QA-style zsRE prompts, attributed to the structural assumption that the last subject token serves as a stable causal hub. The two-phase optimization incurs higher editing latency (about 5s per edit) compared to single-stage editors. Sequential batch editing in lifelong learning scenarios is not addressed.
primary_final_assessment.method_assessment: CPA is a two-phase optimization framework. Phase 1 optimizes a relation anchor at a bottleneck layer to maximize target-object likelihood given the relation feature, with KL regularization. Phase 2 optimizes the subject injection vector to reconstruct the anchored relation feature via a Frobenius-norm loss. The method is editor-agnostic and can be transplanted into existing locate-then-edit pipelines.
primary_final_assessment.quality_rationale: The contribution is clearly scoped to mitigating Subject-Dominant Memory Interference in in-parameter knowledge editing. The diagnosis is supported by gradient saliency and causal tracing analyses. The proposed method is formally motivated and implemented with sufficient detail. Evaluation spans four model backbones and two benchmarks, with ablations confirming the necessity of both phases, mechanistic validation showing restoration of the relational pathway, and plug-and-play results on MEMIT and AlphaEdit. Limitations are explicitly acknowledged, including weaker zsRE performance and increased latency. Related work is positioned appropriately, and claims are consistent with the reported evidence.
primary_final_assessment.scoped_contribution: The paper identifies Subject-Dominant Shortcut as a root cause of memory interference in locate-then-edit knowledge editing and proposes Causal Path Alignment (CPA), a two-phase optimization framework that anchors parameter updates to relation-aware intermediate states to improve relation specificity while minimizing side effects.
